But infinities and their opposites, infinitely tiny values called infinitesimals, became truly significant in the 17th century, spurring one of the most intense scientific debates the world had ever seen.
paras.zh: 关于此类考虑的最古老的已知记录来自阿基米德，他生活在公元前三世纪。但无穷大及其对立面，即被称为无穷小的无穷小值，在 17 世纪变得真正具有重要意义，引发了世界上有史以来最激烈的科学辩论之一。

paras.en: In the 1660s and 1670s, both Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz laid the foundations for what we now call calculus. This branch of mathematics deals with measuring geometric figures and investigating variable quantities, among other things.
paras.zh: 在 1660 年代和 1670 年代，艾萨克·牛顿和戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨为我们现在所说的微积分奠定了基础。该数学分支涉及测量几何图形和研究变量等。

paras.en: At that time, Newton was conducting research at Trinity College Cambridge. Then, in 1665, the bubonic plague swept across Europe, forcing the university to close its doors. Newton dedicated himself even more intensely to his research during this period, making impressive strides in optics and kinematics and even developing a theory of gravitation.
paras.zh: 当时，牛顿正在剑桥三一学院进行研究。然后，1665 年，黑死病席卷欧洲，迫使大学关闭。在此期间，牛顿更加专注于他的研究，在光学和运动学方面取得了令人印象深刻的进步，甚至发展了万有引力理论。

paras.en: The young physicist was particularly fascinated by variable systems. To describe these, however, he needed a new kind of mathematics—which Newton, then in his 20s, invented for this purpose.
paras.zh: 这位年轻的物理学家对可变系统特别着迷。然而，为了描述这些，他需要一种新的数学——当时 20 多岁的牛顿为此目的发明了这种数学。

paras.en: Imagine you drop a ball to the ground. Its velocity will increase over time as the Earth’s gravitational pull accelerates it. The distance, s, traveled by the ball can be described by the equation of motion s = 1/2 gt², where grepresents the acceleration due to gravity, which is 9.81 meters per second squared near Earth’s surface. To keep the formulas as concise as possible, we will omit units and approximate g as 10. This gives us an approximate result of s ≈ 5t² in meters for the distance traveled.
paras.zh: 想象一下你把一个球扔到地上。随着地球引力的加速，它的速度会随着时间的推移而增加。球行进的距离 s 可以用运动方程 s = 1/2 gt² 来描述，其中 代表重力加速度，在地球表面附近为 9.81 米每秒平方。为了使公式尽可能简洁，我们将省略单位并将 g 近似为 10。这为我们提供了行进距离的近似结果 s ≈ 5t²（以米为单位）。

paras.en: But what if we want to know the ball’s speed after it has traveled for one second? We know that the average velocity, v, of an object over a distance traveled is given by the time it takes to travel that distance: v = s/t . But what if the velocity changes continuously and we are interested in v(t) at a specific time, t?
paras.zh: 但是如果我们想知道球运动一秒后的速度怎么办？我们知道，物体在行进一段距离内的平均速度 v 由行进该距离所需的时间给出：v = s/t 。但是，如果速度连续变化并且我们对特定时间 t 的 v(t) 感兴趣怎么办？

paras.en: Newton realized that the result for the instantaneous velocity becomes more accurate when the time interval from which the value is calculated is smaller. To this end, he eventually introduced an “infinitesimal” quantity (dt, in modern notation), which corresponds to a tiny time interval—smaller than any ordinary number.
paras.zh: 牛顿意识到，计算瞬时速度的时间间隔越小，瞬时速度的结果就越准确。为此，他最终引入了一个“无穷小”量（dt，现代表示法），它对应于一个微小的时间间隔——比任何普通数字都要小。

paras.en: The velocity at time t = 1 could therefore be calculated by dividing the distance traveled between t = 1 and t = 1 + dt, written as s(1 + dt) – s(1), by the time interval dt. Substituting the values for t into the distance formula, we obtain: s(1 + dt) = 5(1 + dt)2 = 5 + 10dt + 5(dt)2 and s(t = 1) = 5.
paras.zh: 因此，时间 t = 1 时的速度可以通过将 t = 1 和 t = 1 + dt 之间行进的距离（写为 s(1 + dt) – s(1)）除以时间间隔 dt 来计算。将 t 的值代入距离公式，我们得到： s(1 + dt) = 5(1 + dt)2 = 5 + 10dt + 5(dt)2 和 s(t = 1) = 5。

paras.en: Thus, for the velocity, v, at time t = 1, it follows that: v(t = 1) = (s(1+dt)−s(1)) / dt = (10dt + 5(dt)2) / dt = 10 + 5dt.
paras.zh: 因此，对于时间 t = 1 时的速度 v，可得出： v(t = 1) = (s(1+dt)−s(1)) / dt = (10dt + 5(dt)2) / dt = 10 + 5dt。

paras.en: What does this result, which still depends on dt, mean? According to Newton, it’s 10 meters per second: he simply omitted the dt term.
paras.zh: 这个仍然取决于 dt 的结果意味着什么？根据牛顿的说法，它是每秒 10 米：他只是省略了 dt 术语。

paras.en: About a decade later, philosopher Leibniz considered similar ideas—albeit for entirely different reasons. He was looking for a way to calculate the area under a curve. To do this, he divided the area into increasingly smaller intervals to approximate it by summing the areas of numerous rectangular shapes. The narrower the intervals, the more accurate the calculation becomes. And so Leibniz, too, introduced an infinitesimal: dx.
paras.zh: 大约十年后，哲学家莱布尼茨考虑了类似的想法——尽管出于完全不同的原因。他正在寻找一种计算曲线下面积的方法。为此，他将该区域划分为越来越小的间隔，通过对多个矩形形状的面积求和来近似它。间隔越窄，计算就越准确。因此莱布尼茨也引入了一个无穷小：dx。

paras.en: More detailed investigations of such infinitesimal calculations were then sidelined by a dispute between Leibniz and Newton. Although Leibniz had published his theory before his English colleague, a supporter of Newton—and later Newton himself—claimed that Leibniz had seen his unpublished work on infinitesimal calculus beforehand and had stolen his ideas.
paras.zh: 随后，由于莱布尼茨和牛顿之间的争论，对这种无穷小计算的更详细的研究被搁置了。尽管莱布尼茨在他的英国同事之前发表了他的理论，但牛顿的支持者以及后来的牛顿本人声称莱布尼茨事先看过他未发表的关于微积分的著作并窃取了他的想法。

paras.en: The British Royal Society subsequently launched an investigation that said it had confirmed Newton’s accusations. But Newton himself was president of the society and hand-picked the investigating committee. (Newton, for all his intelligence, is also remembered for ruthlessness; he attacked other brilliant contemporaries, including scientist Robert Hooke.)
paras.zh: 英国皇家学会随后发起调查，称已证实牛顿的指控。但牛顿本人是该协会的主席，并亲自挑选了调查委员会。 (Newton, for all his intelligence, is also remembered for ruthlessness; he attacked other brilliant contemporaries, including scientist Robert Hooke.)

paras.en: Leibniz’s reputation was ruined. He died in 1716, and his grave was unmarked. Only about 75 years later did people add the inscription “OSSA LEIBNITII” (meaning “the bones of Leibniz”).
paras.zh: Leibniz’s reputation was ruined. He died in 1716, and his grave was unmarked.大约75年后，人们才添加了“OSSA LEIBNITII”（意为“莱布尼茨的骨头”）的铭文。

paras.en: Today historians of science agree that there were significant differences between Leibniz’s and Newton’s work on calculus, concluding that both scientists had probably arrived at their findings independently of each other.
paras.zh: 今天，科学史学家一致认为，莱布尼茨和牛顿在微积分方面的工作存在显着差异，并得出结论，两位科学家可能是彼此独立地得出了他们的发现。

paras.en: Next time, I’ll dig into the controversy within the mathematical community surrounding the concept of infinitesimals.
paras.zh: 下一次，我将深入探讨数学界内围绕无穷小概念的争议。

paras.en: This article originally appeared in Spektrum der Wissenschaft and was reproduced with permission. It was translated from the original German version with the assistance of artificial intelligence and reviewed by our editors.
paras.zh: 本文最初发表于 Spektrum der Wissenschaft 并经许可转载。它是在人工智能的帮助下从德语原文翻译而来，并由我们的编辑审阅。

articles.title: Earwax’s surprisingly slippery but sticky properties deters insects
articles.author: Elizabeth Pennisi

paras.en: There are few things more annoying than having a bug fly into your ear. But the body is prepared to fend off these insect invasions, says David Hu, a bioengineer at Georgia Tech.
paras.zh: 没有什么比虫子飞进你的耳朵更烦人的了。但佐治亚理工学院的生物工程师 David Hu 表示，人体已做好抵御这些昆虫入侵的准备。

paras.en: The goop inside our ears may act as a natural insect repellent, Hu’s team reports 28 October in Soft Matter. What we call earwax is not really waxy at all. Instead, the brownish substance absorbs water, a property that might help it regulate moisture in the ear and keep bugs out, the new analysis shows. “[This] familiar biological material may represent a sophisticated physical defense against small arthropods,” says Stanislav Gorb, a functional morphologist at the University of Kiel in Germany, who was not involved with the work.
paras.zh: Hu 的团队于 10 月 28 日在 Soft Matter 杂志上发表报告称，我们耳朵内的粘液可能具有天然驱虫剂的作用。我们所说的耳垢根本不是真正的蜡质。新的分析显示，这种棕色物质会吸收水分，这种特性可能有助于调节耳朵的湿度并防止虫子进入。 “这种熟悉的生物材料可能代表了针对小型节肢动物的复杂物理防御，”德国基尔大学功能形态学家斯坦尼斯拉夫·戈尔布（Stanislav Gorb）说，他没有参与这项工作。

paras.en: Researchers have not studied earwax as much as other body fluids, such as snot, spit or even pee. “It’s a big mystery why we even have [it] in our ears,” Hu says. It can frankly seem like a nuisance. Earwax can build up, clogging earbuds and hearing aids and interfering with hearing, so understanding this substance better may help resolve those problems.
paras.zh: 研究人员对耳垢的研究不如对鼻涕、唾液甚至尿液等其他体液的研究多。 “为什么我们的耳朵里会有它，这是一个很大的谜，”胡说。坦率地说，这看起来很麻烦。耳垢会积聚，堵塞耳塞和助听器并干扰听力，因此更好地了解这种物质可能有助于解决这些问题。

paras.en: Hu and colleagues analyzed the mechanical and chemical properties of 36 earwax samples from pigs, sheep, dogs, cows, rabbits and humans. They also observed how fire ants (Solenopsis invicta) reacted to both natural and synthetic earwax.
paras.zh: Hu 及其同事分析了来自猪、羊、狗、牛、兔子和人类的 36 个耳垢样本的机械和化学特性。他们还观察了火蚁（Solenopsis invicta）对天然和合成耳垢的反应。

paras.en: Even though ants seem able to scale kitchen cabinets with ease to invade countertops, they flounder when they attempt to climb earwax. Hu thinks the earwax sucks moisture from the ants’ feet that helps them grip. But earwax also sticks to ants’ bodies, causing the insects to start grooming incessantly trying to get rid of it. “It’s both sticky and slippery,” Hu says.
paras.zh: 尽管蚂蚁似乎能够轻松地爬过厨房橱柜并侵入工作台面，但当它们试图爬上耳垢时，它们就会陷入困境。胡认为耳垢会吸收蚂蚁足部的水分，帮助它们抓地力。但耳垢也会粘在蚂蚁的身体上，导致蚂蚁开始不断地梳理毛发，试图清除耳垢。 “它既粘又滑，”胡说。

paras.en: The chemical analyses provide some clues about the origins of these properties. Dead skin cells make up 60 percent of earwax, along with a smattering of oils and moisture. The earwax contains pores that Hu believes may be shaped like ink bottles to help it absorb twice its weight in water and prevent water from sloshing around in the ear canal. Like snot, earwax has a huge range of consistencies.
paras.zh: 化学分析提供了有关这些特性起源的一些线索。耳垢的 60% 是由死皮细胞以及少量的油脂和水分组成。胡认为耳垢中含有孔，形状可能像墨水瓶，有助于吸收两倍重量的水，并防止水在耳道中晃动。与鼻涕一样，耳垢也有很大的稠度范围。

paras.en: Under normal conditions, earwax becomes dry and crumbly in about 10 weeks. As it dries, it’s moved outward by a layer of cells lining the ear canal that act as a cleaning conveyor belt. In this way, the ear maintains just the right thickness of earwax to keep insects at bay, Hu says. “It’s most potent when it’s thin,” he explains. “Too much, and the ants can use their tiny claws to grab hold and climb in.”
paras.zh: 正常情况下，耳垢在大约 10 周内就会变得干燥、易碎。当它干燥时，它会被耳道内衬的一层细胞向外移动，充当清洁传送带。胡说，通过这种方式，耳朵可以保持适当的耳垢厚度，以防止昆虫进入。 “当它很薄时，它是最有效的，”他解释道。 “太多了，蚂蚁可以用它们的小爪子抓住并爬进去。”

paras.en: Hu admits there’s no practical way to turn earwax into a commercial insect repellent. Each person has a volume of earwax about equivalent to that of a grain of rice in each ear at any given time, says Hu, so even if you add up all the earwax on Earth, “it’s a pretty rare substance.” But, he adds, companies “are trying to come up with biodegradable and biofriendly ways to deal with insects.” And, says Gorb, perhaps earwax “could inspire a new generation of physical, nontoxic pest control surfaces,” that could provide coatings for protecting stored food, agricultural products and technology.
paras.zh: 胡承认没有实际的方法可以将耳垢变成商业驱虫剂。胡说，每个人在任何特定时间每只耳朵中的耳垢量大约相当于一粒米的量，所以即使你把地球上所有的耳垢加起来，“它也是一种非常稀有的物质。”但是，他补充说，公司“正在努力想出可生物降解和生物友好的方法来对付昆虫。”戈尔布说，也许耳垢“可以激发新一代物理、无毒的害虫防治表面”，为保护储存的食物、农产品和技术提供涂层。

articles.title: Little Ice Age cooling in Europe may have raised the risk of rickets
articles.author: Freda Kreier

paras.en: England isn’t renowned for its weather. But just a few centuries ago, climate change–fueled conditions may have been so bad that they put children’s health at risk.
paras.zh: 英格兰并不以天气而闻名。但就在几个世纪前，气候变化引发的条件可能非常糟糕，以至于使儿童的健康面临风险。

paras.en: Calcium mineralization in the teeth and skeletons of people who lived in rural northern England suggests that children growing up during the height of the Little Ice Age routinely developed vitamin D deficiencies, researchers report November 5 in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology. In the worst cases, these deficiencies developed into rickets, a bone disorder that can occur when people don’t get enough ultraviolet light.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 11 月 5 日在《环境考古学前沿》中报告称，生活在英格兰北部农村地区的人们牙齿和骨骼中的钙矿化表明，在小冰河时期鼎盛时期长大的儿童通常会缺乏维生素 D。在最糟糕的情况下，这些缺陷会发展成佝偻病，这是一种当人们没有获得足够的紫外线时就会发生的骨骼疾病。

paras.en: Previous skeletal studies suggest that rickets became more common among Europeans during the 18th and 19th centuries. One culprit may have been the Industrial Revolution, when many Europeans lived in UV-poor polluted cities and often worked indoors. The unusually cold climate may have added “an extra layer of difficulty” to getting enough sunlight, says Ellen Kendall, a bioarcheologist at Durham University in England
paras.zh: 先前的骨骼研究表明，佝偻病在 18 世纪和 19 世纪的欧洲人中变得更加常见。罪魁祸首之一可能是工业革命，当时许多欧洲人生活在紫外线污染较少的城市，并且经常在室内工作。英国杜伦大学生物考古学家埃伦·肯德尔表示，异常寒冷的气候可能给获得足够的阳光增加了“额外的困难”

paras.en: The Little Ice Age was a period of global cooling from the 13th to 19th centuries caused by extreme solar cycles and a series of volcanic eruptions, which can cool the planet by ejecting aerosols into the atmosphere that block sunlight. In the last 200 years of the era, 18 major eruptions helped spur a temperature drop of 2 to 3 degrees Celsius over northern Europe.
paras.zh: 小冰河时期是13世纪到19世纪的一段全球变冷时期，由极端的太阳周期和一系列火山喷发引起，火山喷发可以通过向大气中喷射阻挡阳光的气溶胶来冷却地球。在这个时代的最后 200 年里，18 次大规模火山喷发导致北欧气温下降了 2 至 3 摄氏度。

paras.en: Kendall and colleagues wondered how this cold climate affected health. They examined calcium deposition — how the essential mineral is incorporated into bones — in the remains of 21 people buried from 1711 to 1829 in the town of North Shields. Calcium often doesn’t fully mineralize in people with vitamin D delicacies, leaving voids in teeth as they grow.
paras.zh: 肯德尔和同事想知道这种寒冷的气候如何影响健康。他们检查了 1711 年至 1829 年间埋葬在北希尔兹镇的 21 具遗骸中的钙沉积情况，即这种必需矿物质如何融入骨骼中。食用维生素 D 美味佳肴的人体内的钙通常无法完全矿化，从而在牙齿生长过程中留下空隙。

paras.en: The team found bands of failed calcium mineralization in the teeth, suggesting seasonal spates of vitamin D deficiencies. Some skeletons also showed signs of rickets. North Shields was a small rural town that hadn’t yet undergone industrialization, so these deficiencies probably weren’t due to bad air conditions.
paras.zh: 研究小组在牙齿中发现了钙矿化失败的带子，这表明维生素 D 存在季节性缺乏。一些骨骼还表现出佝偻病的迹象。北希尔兹是一个尚未实现工业化的乡村小镇，所以这些缺陷可能不是由于空气条件恶劣造成的。

paras.en: The unusually cold weather may have changed people’s behavior during the winter, Kendall says. Residents may have kept their kids indoors or bundled them up so that little skin was exposed when they did go outside, preventing them from getting enough UV light, she says.
paras.zh: 肯德尔说，异常寒冷的天气可能改变了人们在冬季的行为。她说，居民可能把孩子留在室内或把他们裹得严严实实，这样当他们出去时就很少有皮肤暴露，从而阻止他们接受足够的紫外线。

paras.en: However, climate was still just one factor among many — including gender roles, diet and pollution — that shaped vitamin D deficiencies at the time, says Kendall. “Humans are very messy to study,” she says. “That’s one of the things that makes them so very fascinating.”
paras.zh: 然而，肯德尔说，气候仍然只是当时导致维生素 D 缺乏的众多因素之一，包括性别角色、饮食和污染。 “人类的研究非常混乱，”她说。 “这就是让它们如此迷人的原因之一。”

articles.title: This armored amphibian once lived and hunted on the seafloor
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: Most amphibians shrivel or suffocate in saltwater. But long ago, an oddball armored amphibian may have dwelled deep in the ocean.
paras.zh: 大多数两栖动物在盐水中会枯萎或窒息。但很久以前，一种奇怪的装甲两栖动物可能居住在海洋深处。

paras.en: Scientists have found evidence that an ancient amphibian with a flattened body and upturned eyes may have once stalked the seafloor. The animal, Gerrothorax maritimus, is the first ever amphibian known to have lived without access to land or freshwater, researchers report October 26 in Nature Ecology & Evolution.
paras.zh: 科学家发现的证据表明，一种身体扁平、眼睛向上的古代两栖动物可能曾经在海底潜行。研究人员于 10 月 26 日在《自然生态学与进化》杂志上发表报告称，这种名为 Gerrothorax maritimus 的动物是已知的第一种在没有陆地或淡水的情况下生活的两栖动物。

paras.en: G. maritimus, which lived 237 million years ago, was rather unlike today’s amphibians, which breathe and drink through their porous skin. The creature’s lifestyle was unimaginable for an amphibian, says Ryosuke Motani, a paleobiologist at the University of California, Davis. Of the more than 8,000 amphibians known today, none live solely in saltwater.
paras.zh: G. maritimus 生活在 2.37 亿年前，与今天的两栖动物截然不同，它们通过多孔的皮肤呼吸和饮水。加州大学戴维斯分校的古生物学家 Motani Ryosuke Motani 表示，这种生物的生活方式对于两栖动物来说是难以想象的。当今已知的 8,000 多种两栖动物中，没有一种只生活在咸水中。

paras.en: Motani and his colleagues inspected two well-preserved G. maritimus fossils from the late Triassic Period, which spanned roughly 237 million to 201 million years ago. Each creature measured around 70 centimeters, about as long as a skateboard, and was swathed in armor made of bony plates. The specimens appeared nearly identical to their closest relatives, other amphibians that dwelled in freshwater, Motani says. But the fossils’ location was unusual: They were found in what was once a seabed, roughly 30 kilometers from any ancient land.
paras.zh: Motani 和他的同事检查了两块保存完好的三叠纪晚期的 G. maritimus 化石，该时期的时间跨度约为 2.37 亿年至 2.01 亿年前。每个生物长约 70 厘米，大约有滑板那么长，并包裹着由骨板制成的盔甲。莫塔尼说，这些标本与它们的近亲、生活在淡水中的其他两栖动物几乎一模一样。但这些化石的位置很不寻常：它们是在曾经的海底发现的，距离任何古代陆地大约 30 公里。

paras.en: It wasn’t clear whether the creatures lived in the ocean or were landlubbers that got buried there after they perished. So the team performed a chemical analysis. Levels of different forms of strontium in the fossil bones matched those of the Triassic ocean. This telltale sign revealed that G. maritimus ate seafood and drank seawater. “That means it lived there,” Motani says.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚这些生物是生活在海洋中，还是死后被埋在那里的旱鸭子。因此，研究小组进行了化学分析。骨骼化石中不同形式的锶含量与三叠纪海洋中的锶含量相匹配。这个迹象表明，G. maritimus 吃海鲜、喝海水。 “这意味着它住在那里，”莫塔尼说。

paras.en: For amphibians, “this is the first time that that we have hard evidence that they were actually adapted for long-term life in the sea,” says Lachlan Hart, a paleobiologist at the University of New South Wales in Sydney who was not involved with the new study. Hart and his colleagues previously suggested that a different ancient amphibian may have been seafaring but probably did not dwell in the ocean.
paras.zh: 对于两栖动物来说，“这是我们第一次有确凿的证据表明它们实际上适合在海洋中长期生活，”悉尼新南威尔士大学的古生物学家拉克兰·哈特（Lachlan Hart）说，他没有参与这项新研究。哈特和他的同事此前提出，另一种古代两栖动物可能一直在航海，但可能并不居住在海洋中。

paras.en: Scientists have long searched for a marine amphibian. The fossil record is littered with skeletal fragments revealing how some mammals, reptiles and birds have adapted to a salty lifestyle. “Amphibians were always the problem because they did not really follow the rule,” Motani says.
paras.zh: 科学家们长期以来一直在寻找海洋两栖动物。化石记录中散布着骨骼碎片，揭示了一些哺乳动物、爬行动物和鸟类如何适应含盐的生活方式。 “两栖动物始终是个问题，因为它们没有真正遵守规则，”莫塔尼说。

paras.en: The same skin that makes today’s amphibians vulnerable to disease and toxins also makes saltwater fearsome. Key adaptations allowed G. maritimus to skirt these issues. G. maritimus and its relatives evolved bony body armor, probably for defense. But these hard plates would have helped the seafloor dwellers prevent water loss. And unlike modern amphibians, which typically lose their internal gills after the larval stage, this creature and its close relatives retained a fishy breathing strategy suitable for life in the depths.
paras.zh: 使当今两栖动物容易感染疾病和毒素的皮肤也使盐水变得可怕。关键的适应性改变使得 G. maritimus 能够避开这些问题。 G. maritimus 及其亲属进化出了骨质防弹衣，可能是为了防御。但这些坚硬的板块可以帮助海底居民防止水分流失。与现代两栖动物不同的是，现代两栖动物通常在幼虫阶段后就会失去内鳃，这种生物及其近亲保留了适合深海生活的鱼腥味呼吸策略。

paras.en: G. maritimus fossils hint that the animal lurked on the seafloor as an ambush predator. Its jaw lifted upward like a toilet seat so that it could unleash a suction attack on fish and other small creatures.
paras.zh: G. maritimus 化石表明，这种动物作为伏击掠食者潜伏在海底。它的下巴像马桶座圈一样向上抬起，这样就可以对鱼类和其他小生物发动吸力攻击。

paras.en: There may yet be other amphibians hiding in ancient oceans, environments ignored by paleontologists studying these creatures. “Because they’re amphibians, we would be looking for them in terrestrial freshwater environments,” Hart says. Perhaps there are more amphibians that have gotten their sea legs.
paras.zh: 古代海洋中可能还隐藏着其他两栖动物，而研究这些生物的古生物学家却忽视了这些环境。 “因为它们是两栖动物，我们会在陆地淡水环境中寻找它们，”哈特说。或许还有更多的两栖动物已经适应了水下环境。

articles.title: Here's Why The Dire Wolf Really Wasn't Brought Back From Extinction, Scientists Argue
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: When is a de-extinction not a de-extinction? Some headline-grabbing methods for bringing extinct species back to life fall short of such grand claims, according to a new argument published in Biology Letters.
paras.zh: 什么时候“复灭绝”不是“复灭绝”？根据《生物学快报》发表的一项新论点，一些引人注目的使灭绝物种复活的方法并没有达到如此宏伟的要求。

paras.en: The case is put forward by marine biologist Andrew Davinack and biochemist Charlotte Daniels from Wheaton College Massachusetts, with much of their attention focused on the so-called 'de-extinction' of the dire wolf by biotech company Colossal Biosciences in 2025.
paras.zh: 这个案例是由马萨诸塞州惠顿学院的海洋生物学家安德鲁·达维纳克和生物化学家夏洛特·丹尼尔斯提出的，他们的大部分注意力都集中在生物技术公司 Colossal Biosciences 于 2025 年所谓的恐狼“灭绝”上。

paras.en: What Colossal Biosciences did was make genetic edits to grey wolf cells in order to breed animals with characteristics that more closely resembled dire wolves – including larger bodies, bigger teeth, and paler coats of fur.
paras.zh: Colossal Biosciences 所做的就是对灰狼细胞进行基因编辑，以培育出具有更接近恐狼特征的动物，包括更大的身体、更大的牙齿和更苍白的皮毛。

paras.en: That's actually not a de-extinction, Davinack and Daniels contest, and they've got a new term for the mistake of calling it one: lineage-genome conflation.
paras.zh: 达维纳克和丹尼尔斯争论说，这实际上并不是一场“反灭绝”运动，他们为错误的说法起了一个新术语：谱系-基因组合并。

paras.en: "Recent advances in ancient DNA sequencing, comparative genomics and genome editing have renewed interest in de-extinction, often framed as the technological reversal of species loss," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“古代 DNA 测序、比较基因组学和基因组编辑方面的最新进展重新激发了人们对反灭绝的兴趣，这通常被视为物种灭绝的技术逆转。”

paras.en: "Here, we argue that de-extinction cannot recover extinct species because extinction represents the termination of an evolutionary lineage, not merely the disappearance of genetic information."
paras.zh: “在这里，我们认为反灭绝无法恢复灭绝的物种，因为灭绝代表着进化谱系的终止，而不仅仅是遗传信息的消失。”

paras.en: There are several parts to the argument. The researchers point out that a species is more than its DNA – that genes and the physical characteristics they result in have been born from a long, continuous, evolutionary history. Any gaps in that history break the connection and redefine the species.
paras.zh: 这个论点有几个部分。研究人员指出，一个物种不仅仅是它的 DNA，基因及其产生的物理特征是在漫长、连续的进化历史中诞生的。历史上的任何空白都会打破联系并重新定义物种。

paras.en: Then we have the issues of habitats and populations. Can just a few engineered animals recreate the variation of a large population, or the historical habitat it was part of? Davinack and Daniels suggest not.
paras.zh: 然后我们还有栖息地和人口的问题。仅仅少数转基因动物就能重现大量种群的变异，或其所属的历史栖息地吗？达维纳克和丹尼尔斯建议不要。

paras.en: To go back to the dire wolves example, these wolves were living in a very different world to today's more than 10,000 years ago. The climate, food sources, predators, and other environmental connections are no longer around in the modern day – another break that makes the extinction permanent.
paras.zh: 回到恐狼的例子，一万多年前，这些狼生活在一个与今天截然不同的世界。气候、食物来源、捕食者和其他环境联系在现代已不复存在——这是导致灭绝永久化的另一个突破。

paras.en: "Species are historically continuous population-level lineages shaped by gene flow, mutation, drift, selection, demographic history and ecological interaction," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“物种是历史上连续的种群谱系，由基因流动、突变、漂变、选择、人口历史和生态相互作用形成。”

paras.en: "A reconstructed genome, even if highly accurate, represents at most a partial snapshot of an individual organism."
paras.zh: “重建的基因组，即使非常准确，也最多代表单个生物体的部分快照。”

paras.en: The researchers acknowledge that many scientists, and the studies authored by them, are careful not to use terms like 'de-extinction' when they aren't accurate. However, they are asking for private companies and media outlets to be more responsible when reporting these advances in technology.
paras.zh: 研究人员承认，许多科学家以及他们撰写的研究都小心翼翼地避免使用“去灭绝”等不准确的术语。然而，他们要求私营公司和媒体在报道这些技术进步时更加负责任。

paras.en: Terms like de-extinction can be misleading and misrepresent the science involved, the researchers argue, which then makes it harder to put technological progress and new techniques in context.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，像“去灭绝”这样的术语可能会产生误导，并歪曲所涉及的科学，这使得将技术进步和新技术置于背景中变得更加困难。

paras.en: "Greater precision in terminology therefore has practical consequences," write the researchers. "Lineage restoration, genetic recovery, phenotypic reconstruction, ecological substitution and restoration of historical communities are distinct objectives and require different criteria of success."
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“因此，术语更加精确会产生实际影响。” “谱系恢复、遗传恢复、表型重建、生态替代和历史群落的恢复是不同的目标，需要不同的成功标准。”

paras.en: The researchers don't go as far as saying de-extinction is impossible, but they do contend that the dire wolves case doesn't qualify. Using preserved cells or preserved embryos is a more promising route for de-extinction, the researchers say – solving some of the problems mentioned above, and ensuring greater "biological continuity".
paras.zh: 研究人员并没有说消除灭绝是不可能的，但他们确实认为恐狼的案例不符合条件。研究人员表示，使用保存的细胞或保存的胚胎是一种更有希望的灭绝灭绝途径，可以解决上述一些问题，并确保更大的“生物连续性”。

paras.en: Scientists used the cell preservation technique with the Pyrenean ibex back in 2003, and although the animal didn't survive, there's a stronger claim to de-extinction.
paras.zh: 早在 2003 年，科学家们就对比利牛斯山野山羊使用了细胞保存技术，尽管这种动物最终没能存活下来，但人们更有力地主张“复活”。

paras.en: It's worth pointing out that the researchers aren't arguing that the work done by companies such as Colossal Biosciences is without merit as far as genetic engineering goes – but that we need to be careful when describing and evaluating it.
paras.zh: 值得指出的是，研究人员并不是说 Colossal Biosciences 等公司所做的工作在基因工程方面没有任何价值，而是说我们在描述和评估它时需要小心。

paras.en: So, rather than bringing back dire wolves from extinction, what we actually saw in 2025 were grey wolves with some dire wolf traits – not the resurrection of the species.
paras.zh: 因此，我们在 2025 年实际看到的并不是恐狼从灭绝中复活，而是具有某些恐狼特征的灰狼，而不是该物种的复活。

paras.en: "Genomic reconstruction may recreate selected traits or produce ecological proxies, but it cannot recover extinct species as historically continuous evolutionary lineages," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“基因组重建可能会重建选定的性状或产生生态代理，但它无法将灭绝的物种恢复为历史上连续的进化谱系。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Biology Letters.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《生物学快报》上。

articles.title: Gravity May Protect The Universe From Time Travel Paradoxes, But There's a Catch
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: If, for whatever reason, by whatever means, you travel back in time, you absolutely must not find and kill your own grandfather before he has had a chance to procreate.
paras.zh: 如果，无论出于何种原因，无论以何种方式，你穿越回过去，你绝对不能在你自己的祖父有机会繁衍之前找到并杀死他。

paras.en: Doing so would break the Universe – because if your grandfather never has offspring, you would not be born and could not travel back in time to kill him.
paras.zh: 这样做会破坏宇宙——因为如果你的祖父没有后代，你就不会出生，也无法回到过去杀死他。

paras.en: Quite how the Universe would resolve this conundrum is unclear. Maybe the laws of physics would simply prevent it from happening in the first place. Stephen Hawking said so.
paras.zh: 宇宙将如何解决这个难题尚不清楚。也许物理定律会从一开始就阻止它发生。史蒂芬·霍金如是说。

paras.en: But today, we have good news. Physicists have found a mathematical way to avert this crisis. There's just one little problem: their solution introduces an instability that could cause tiny disturbances in the fabric of spacetime to grow exponentially.
paras.zh: 但今天，我们有好消息。物理学家找到了一种数学方法来避免这场危机。只有一个小问题：他们的解决方案引入了一种不稳定性，可能会导致时空结构中的微小扰动呈指数级增长。

paras.en: Hawking proposed his chronology protection conjecture in 1992 to explore the question of whether backward time travel was even possible. The conjecture states, "The laws of physics do not allow the appearance of closed timelike curves."
paras.zh: 霍金于1992年提出了时间顺序保护猜想，以探索向后时间旅行是否可能的问题。该猜想指出：“物理定律不允许出现闭合类时曲线。”

paras.en: The problem is that, although Hawking's calculations supported his conjecture, physicists have yet to establish that the Universe actually enforces it.
paras.zh: 问题在于，尽管霍金的计算支持了他的猜想，但物理学家尚未证实宇宙实际上强制执行了这一猜想。

paras.en: Einstein's general theory of relativity, our best description of gravity, allows for some decidedly peculiar arrangements of spacetime. Among them are closed timelike curves – paths through spacetime that, at least mathematically, can lead a traveler back to their own past.
paras.zh: 爱因斯坦的广义相对论是我们对引力的最好描述，它允许一些明显奇特的时空安排。其中包括封闭的类时曲线——穿过时空的路径，至少在数学上，可以引导旅行者回到自己的过去。

paras.en: Whether such paths could actually exist in the physical Universe is another matter entirely.
paras.zh: 这样的路径是否真的存在于物理宇宙中完全是另一回事。

paras.en: Hawking suspected that quantum effects would prevent them from forming. But nobody has managed to conclusively identify what that mechanism might be.
paras.zh: 霍金怀疑量子效应会阻止它们的形成。但没有人能够最终确定这种机制可能是什么。

paras.en: Physicists Moustafa Ismail and David Mattingly of the University of New Hampshire wondered whether gravity itself might hold the answer. After all, if the mathematics of gravity allows time loops to exist, perhaps a different formulation of gravity could prevent them.
paras.zh: 新罕布什尔大学的物理学家穆斯塔法·伊斯梅尔和大卫·马丁利想知道重力本身是否能找到答案。毕竟，如果引力数学允许时间循环存在，也许不同的引力公式可以阻止它们。

paras.en: Now, there's something you need to understand about gravity. Although general relativity is the best framework we currently have for describing it, it's not the only framework we have for describing it.
paras.zh: 现在，您需要了解一些关于重力的事情。尽管广义相对论是我们目前描述它的最佳框架，但它并不是我们描述它的唯一框架。

paras.en: In general relativity, spacetime has a geometry described by something called a metric, which determines distances and intervals of time, and a mathematical connection that describes how directions change as you move through that geometry. The two are linked in a particular way.
paras.zh: 在广义相对论中，时空具有由称为度量的东西描述的几何形状，它确定距离和时间间隔，以及描述当您在该几何形状中移动时方向如何变化的数学联系。两者以特定的方式联系在一起。

paras.en: An alternative framework for gravity called metric-affine gravity loosens that relationship, allowing the metric and the connection to operate more independently.
paras.zh: 一种称为度量仿射引力的替代引力框架放松了这种关系，允许度量和连接更加独立地运行。

paras.en: This is where Ismail and Mattingly found some wiggle room.
paras.zh: 这就是伊斯梅尔和马丁利找到一些回旋余地的地方。

paras.en: They used metric-affine gravity to construct a model in which spacetime could have a built-in direction of time. Under the right conditions, time would always move forward along any path a traveler could take through spacetime, making it impossible to loop back into their own past.
paras.zh: 他们使用度量仿射引力构建了一个模型，在该模型中时空可以具有内置的时间方向。在适当的条件下，时间总是会沿着旅行者可以穿越时空的任何路径向前移动，使得他们不可能回到自己的过去。

paras.en: They named this model Metric-Affine Gravity Imposing Chronology. That's right. MAGIC.
paras.zh: 他们将这个模型命名为“公制仿射重力强加年表”。这是正确的。魔法。

paras.en: In general relativity, gravity can fluctuate in two different ways, corresponding to the two ways gravitational waves can stretch and squeeze space.
paras.zh: 在广义相对论中，引力可以以两种不同的方式波动，对应于引力波拉伸和挤压空间的两种方式。

paras.en: MAGIC introduces a third way for gravity to fluctuate – the scalar mode. And the scalar mode doesn't play particularly nicely with reality as we know it.
paras.zh: MAGIC 引入了第三种重力波动方式——标量模式。正如我们所知，标量模式并不能很好地适应现实。

paras.en: On the cosmological background the researchers studied, it suffers from something called a gradient instability. Rather than propagating as stable waves normally do, disturbances in MAGIC's scalar mode can grow exponentially, with shorter wavelengths growing faster.
paras.zh: 在研究人员研究的宇宙学背景下，它遭受了所谓的梯度不稳定性的困扰。 MAGIC 标量模式中的扰动不会像正常的稳定波那样传播，而是会呈指数增长，其中波长较短的增长速度更快。

paras.en: This means that, in its current form, MAGIC cannot provide a stable description of the Universe.
paras.zh: 这意味着，以目前的形式，MAGIC 无法提供对宇宙的稳定描述。

paras.en: That's the biggest obstacle to making MAGIC a viable theory of gravity. There are some smaller ones, too.
paras.zh: 这是使 MAGIC 成为可行的引力理论的最大障碍。还有一些较小的。

paras.en: First, MAGIC only establishes the conditions for chronology protection locally.
paras.zh: 首先，MAGIC仅在本地建立了时间顺序保护的条件。

paras.en: To guarantee that time can't loop back on itself anywhere in the Universe, the researchers have to make an additional assumption about the overall structure of spacetime that they haven't shown follows from the model itself.
paras.zh: 为了保证时间不会在宇宙中的任何地方自行循环，研究人员必须对时空的整体结构做出额外的假设，但他们尚未证明模型本身是否遵循这一假设。

paras.en: So while they can make MAGIC prevent time loops, they have not yet shown that time loop prevention is baked into MAGIC itself.
paras.zh: 因此，虽然他们可以让 MAGIC 防止时间循环，但他们尚未表明时间循环预防已融入 MAGIC 本身。

paras.en: Second, MAGIC is designed to prevent the metric from breaking down in ways that would make spacetime impossible to describe properly – but this safeguard doesn't work in every circumstance.
paras.zh: 其次，MAGIC 旨在防止度量因无法正确描述时空而崩溃，但这种保护措施并非在所有情况下都有效。

paras.en: We don't know that these breakdowns do actually occur in MAGIC – the researchers haven't demonstrated that they do – but they haven't ruled them out, either.
paras.zh: 我们不知道这些故障是否真的发生在 MAGIC 中——研究人员还没有证明它们确实发生——但他们也没有排除这种可能性。

paras.en: So, we have a framework that is designed to do specific things that may not always do the specific things.
paras.zh: 因此，我们有一个框架，旨在执行特定的操作，但可能并不总是执行特定的操作。

paras.en: But that's OK. Because MAGIC isn't supposed to be the final answer. It's an intriguing demonstration of how chronology protection might be built into gravity – a step in a research direction, not a working solution yet.
paras.zh: 但没关系。因为 MAGIC 不应该是最终答案。这是一个有趣的演示，展示了如何将年代学保护构建到重力中——这是研究方向的一步，但还不是一个可行的解决方案。

paras.en: And, having taken that step, the researchers have a clearer idea of where to go next.
paras.zh: 而且，迈出这一步后，研究人员对下一步该何去何从有了更清晰的想法。

paras.en: "Stabilizing the scalar without losing the timelike, closed projective mode is the natural next step toward a phenomenological completion," they write.
paras.zh: 他们写道：“稳定标量而不失去类似时间的封闭射影模式是迈向现象学完成的自然下一步。”

paras.en: So tell your grandpa to sit tight. Physicists might find a way to save his bacon from time-traveling, rule-breaking grandchildren yet.
paras.zh: 所以告诉你爷爷稳住。物理学家可能会找到一种方法来拯救他的培根免受时间旅行、违反规则的孙辈的侵害。

paras.en: The research has been published in Physical Review D.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《物理评论 D》上。

articles.title: Scientists Discover Two Remarkably Untouched Worlds Hidden in The Pacific
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: What would the ocean look like if humans had barely touched it?
paras.zh: 如果人类几乎没有接触过海洋，它会是什么样子？

paras.en: It's not easy to tell. Our marine environment is in a state of perilous transformation, threatened by wildlife extinctions, coral deterioration, and worsening levels of pollution, acidity, and heat.
paras.zh: 这并不容易说清楚。我们的海洋环境正处于危险的转变状态，受到野生动物灭绝、珊瑚退化以及污染、酸度和热量不断恶化的威胁。

paras.en: But while there aren't many places left on Earth where the ocean looks untouched, far out in the Pacific, two isolated havens have been hiding something extraordinary.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管地球上没有多少地方的海洋看起来未受破坏，但在遥远的太平洋上，两个偏僻的避风港却隐藏着一些非凡的东西。

paras.en: In a new study in Frontiers in Marine Science, scientists surveyed the Bikar and Bokak coral atolls, which last year were declared the first national marine sanctuary in the Marshall Islands.
paras.zh: 在《海洋科学前沿》的一项新研究中，科学家们调查了比卡尔和博卡克珊瑚环礁，这些珊瑚环礁去年被宣布为马绍尔群岛第一个国家海洋保护区。

paras.en: There is good reason to enforce protection of these special places, as they represent some of the most intact ecosystems remaining in the region, according to marine ecologist Alan Friedlander from the University of Hawai'i.
paras.zh: 夏威夷大学的海洋生态学家艾伦·弗里德兰德 (Alan Friedlander) 表示，有充分的理由加强对这些特殊地点的保护，因为它们代表了该地区剩余的一些最完整的生态系统。

paras.en: "Bikar and Bokak are not just treasures for the Marshall Islands but for the entire planet, a gift from the community of Utirik Atoll, which has traditionally and vigilantly safeguarded these fragile ecosystems for decades," Friedlander says.
paras.zh: 弗里德兰德说：“比卡尔和博卡克不仅是马绍尔群岛的宝藏，也是整个地球的宝藏，是乌蒂里克环礁社区的礼物，几十年来，乌蒂里克环礁社区一直以传统方式警惕地保护着这些脆弱的生态系统。”

paras.en: While traditional Marshallese communities have known about Bikar and Bokak for centuries, their extreme remoteness from humans has left them uniquely unspoiled.
paras.zh: 虽然传统的马绍尔社区几个世纪以来就知道比卡尔和博卡克，但由于它们距离人类极其遥远，所以它们没有受到破坏。

paras.en: Bikar is situated over 100 kilometers (62 miles) from the nearest inhabited atoll, and Bokak lies even further, at almost 400 kilometers away from people.
paras.zh: 比卡尔距离最近有人居住的环礁超过 100 公里（62 英里），而博卡克距离更远，距离人类近 400 公里。

paras.en: The new findings stem from a 2023 research expedition to study the atolls, aiming to give us our best understanding yet of their ecosystems.
paras.zh: 这些新发现源于 2023 年对环礁进行的一次研究考察，旨在让我们更好地了解其生态系统。

paras.en: "Remote oceanic atolls provide some of the last opportunities to examine ecological structure and functioning in systems where predator assemblages, seabird colonies, native vegetation, and cross-habitat ecological processes remain comparatively less affected by direct local human pressures," Friedlander and fellow researchers write in their paper.
paras.zh: 弗里德兰德和其他研究人员在论文中写道：“偏远的海洋环礁为研究系统中的生态结构和功能提供了最后的机会，在这些系统中，捕食者组合、海鸟群、本地植被和跨栖息地生态过程受当地人类直接压力的影响相对较小。”

paras.en: "By integrating observations from land to the deep sea, this study provides one of the most comprehensive ecosystem assessments conducted for remote central Pacific atolls and offers rare insight into the structure of relatively intact tropical marine ecosystems in the Anthropocene."
paras.zh: “通过整合从陆地到深海的观测，这项研究提供了对偏远的中央太平洋环礁进行的最全面的生态系统评估之一，并为人类世相对完整的热带海洋生态系统的结构提供了罕见的见解。”

paras.en: The field expeditions – which helped inform and secure Bikar and Bokak's protected status – observed 266 reef fish taxa from 38 families, with greater biomass of fish seen at Bokak.
paras.zh: 实地考察帮助了解并确保了比卡尔和博卡克的受保护地位，观察到了来自 38 个科的 266 个珊瑚礁鱼类类群，其中在博卡克发现了更大的鱼类生物量。

paras.en: Sharks were a standout, representing the biggest individual component of fore-reef biomass, accounting for 26.8 percent at Bikar and 33.9 percent at Bokak.
paras.zh: 鲨鱼是其中的佼佼者，代表了前礁生物量的最大个体组成部分，占比卡尔的 26.8% 和博卡克的 33.9%。

paras.en: Using submersibles, the scientists documented 138 fish taxa living at greater depths (up to 275 meters), with the researchers noting 14 of the groups appeared to represent previously unreported records for the Marshall Islands. Deep-sea cameras observed an additional 79 groups of fishes living at even lower depths.
paras.zh: 科学家们利用潜水器记录了生活在更深处（最深 275 米）的 138 个鱼类类群，研究人员指出，其中 14 个类群似乎代表了马绍尔群岛之前未报告的记录。深海摄像机还观察到生活在更低深度的另外 79 群鱼类。

paras.en: The researchers also documented 17 seabird species across the atolls, and recorded 71 turtle crawls and 132 turtle nest pits, concentrated largely at Bikar.
paras.zh: 研究人员还记录了环礁上的 17 种海鸟，并记录了 71 次海龟爬行和 132 个海龟巢坑，主要集中在比卡尔。

paras.en: "These atolls have extensive seabird colonies, mature native vegetation, active turtle nesting, high reef-fish biomass and large predators, coral-dominated reefs at Bokak, structurally complex mesophotic habitats, and surprisingly diverse and poorly known deep-sea communities," Friedlander says.
paras.zh: 弗里德兰德说：“这些环礁拥有广泛的海鸟栖息地、成熟的本土植被、活跃的海龟筑巢、高珊瑚鱼生物量和大型捕食者、博卡克以珊瑚为主的珊瑚礁、结构复杂的中光栖息地，以及令人惊讶的多样化和鲜为人知的深海群落。”

paras.en: "They are among the best ecological reference systems we have to better understand what we have lost elsewhere and to provide fundamental insights needed for effective conservation and restoration efforts."
paras.zh: “它们是最好的生态参考系统之一，我们必须更好地了解我们在其他地方失去的东西，并为有效的保护和恢复工作提供所需的基本见解。”

paras.en: Even among these remote Pacific atolls, however, signs of ecological interference are visible.
paras.zh: 然而，即使在这些偏远的太平洋环礁中，生态干扰的迹象也显而易见。

paras.en: At the time of the 2023 surveys, both Bikar and Bokak contained populations of introduced Polynesian rats (Rattus exulans), and while the atolls enjoy considerable isolation from human influences, they are not shielded from the global trends of warming waters, coral bleaching, and ocean acidification.
paras.zh: 在 2023 年进行调查时，比卡尔和博卡克都有引进的波利尼西亚老鼠 (Rattus exulans) 种群，虽然环礁与人类的影响相当隔离，但它们并没有免受全球海水变暖、珊瑚白化和海洋酸化趋势的影响。

paras.en: "We use 'relatively intact' as a comparative description rather than as an assumption that remote reefs represent pristine or historically undisturbed states," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们使用‘相对完整’作为比较描述，而不是假设偏远的珊瑚礁代表原始或历史上未受干扰的状态。”

paras.en: "Remoteness can reduce some forms of direct local human pressure, but it does not eliminate historical, introduced, or global anthropogenic influences, and ecological condition should therefore be evaluated from observed ecosystem attributes rather than remoteness alone."
paras.zh: “偏远可以减少某些形式的直接当地人类压力，但它并不能消除历史的、引入的或全球的人为影响，因此，生态条件应该根据观察到的生态系统属性来评估，而不仅仅是偏远。”

paras.en: But even if Bikar and Bokak are not completely untouched, they're about as untouched as it gets.
paras.zh: 但即使比卡尔和博卡克并非完全没有受到影响，他们也几乎没有受到影响。

paras.en: And that means we need to study and learn all we can about these special places, because the sad truth is that most coral atolls do not look like this anymore, because of human activity.
paras.zh: 这意味着我们需要尽我们所能地研究和了解这些特殊的地方，因为可悲的事实是，由于人类活动，大多数珊瑚环礁不再像这样了。

paras.en: In a stark illustration of the contrasts, just days after surveying Bokak in 2023, the research expedition moved onto Bikini Atoll, the notorious site of US nuclear tests in the mid–20th century.
paras.zh: 2023 年对博卡克进行勘察几天后，研究考察队就转移到了比基尼环礁，这里是美国在 20 世纪中叶进行核试验的臭名昭著的地点，这就是鲜明的对比。

paras.en: "In those years, the bombing vaporized three islands and left behind radioactive contamination that, to this day, leaves the atoll uninhabitable," an expedition member wrote in a field diary.
paras.zh: 一名探险队成员在野外日记中写道：“那些年，轰炸使三个岛屿蒸发，留下了放射性污染，直到今天，环礁仍无法居住。”

paras.en: "Overall the feeling is somber here. Things just feel a bit off. The first dives found some fish and a few spots with live coral, but also a lot of pulverized, dead reef with not much living on it."
paras.zh: “总的来说，这里的感觉很阴沉。感觉有点不对劲。第一次潜水发现了一些鱼和一些有活珊瑚的地方，但也有很多粉状的死礁石，上面没有太多生物。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Frontiers in Marine Science.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《海洋科学前沿》上。

articles.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian

paras.en: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
paras.zh: 2.37 亿年前的化石揭示了一种奇异的装甲海洋两栖动物

paras.en: - A bizarre, heavily armored amphibian roamed the oceans 237 million years ago, despite the fact that modern amphibians cannot survive entirely in saltwater. Discovered in China, the giant salamander-sized creature may be the first known amphibian to have adapted to a fully marine existence.
paras.zh: - 2.37 亿年前，尽管现代两栖动物无法完全在盐水中生存，但一种奇特的重甲两栖动物在海洋中漫游。这种大鲵大小的生物在中国发现，可能是已知的第一种完全适应海洋生存的两栖动物。

paras.en: A remarkable fossil discovery in China has revealed an ancient amphibian that lived entirely in the ocean, something no amphibian alive today is known to do. The unusual animal, named Gerrothorax maritimus, had a broad, flattened body protected by bony armor and was roughly the size of a giant salamander. Researchers believe it spent much of its life on the seafloor, waiting to ambush passing prey.
paras.zh: 中国的一项非凡化石发现揭示了一种完全生活在海洋中的古代两栖动物，这是目前还没有现存两栖动物能做到的。这种不寻常的动物被称为Gerrothorax maritimus，它有一个宽阔、扁平的身体，有骨甲保护，大小与大鲵差不多。研究人员认为，它一生的大部分时间都在海底度过，等待伏击路过的猎物。

paras.en: The discovery comes from an international team at the University of California, Davis, Peking University, and the Geological Museum of Guizhou. Their findings, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, are based on two exceptionally well-preserved skeletons dating back nearly 237 million years to the Late Triassic period.
paras.zh: 这一发现来自加州大学戴维斯分校、北京大学和贵州地质博物馆的一个国际团队。他们的研究结果发表在《自然生态学与进化》杂志上，基于两具保存异常完好的骨骼，其历史可以追溯到近 2.37 亿年前的三叠纪晚期。

paras.en: Both fossils were uncovered in China's Guizhou Province, in a region that was once submerged beneath an ancient ocean hundreds of miles from major landmasses.
paras.zh: 这两块化石都是在中国贵州省发现的，该地区曾经淹没在距离主要陆地数百英里的古老海洋之下。

paras.en: "This area is part of an ecosystem that we've been looking at and trying to reconstruct," said study corresponding author Ryosuke Motani, a professor in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at UC Davis. "We've been mostly studying marine reptiles and the fish from this place, but now we also have this amphibian, and it's a sort of very unusual member of the lineage."
paras.zh: 研究通讯作者、加州大学戴维斯分校地球与行星科学系教授 Motani Ryosuke Motani 表示：“这个区域是我们一直在研究并试图重建的生态系统的一部分。” “我们主要研究海洋爬行动物和来自这个地方的鱼类，但现在我们也有这种两栖动物，它是该谱系中一种非常不寻常的成员。”

paras.en: The finding is especially surprising because amphibians are generally unable to survive in seawater. Among the more than 8,000 amphibian species living today, none are known to spend their entire lives in marine environments, and fewer than 2% have any ability to tolerate salt.
paras.zh: 这一发现尤其令人惊讶，因为两栖动物通常无法在海水中生存。在当今生活的 8,000 多种两栖动物中，没有一种是终生生活在海洋环境中的，只有不到 2% 的两栖动物具有耐盐能力。

paras.en: Mammals, reptiles, and birds, by comparison, all include species that can live entirely at sea without relying on land for food or fresh water. Until this discovery, scientists had never identified convincing fossil evidence of an amphibian with the same ability.
paras.zh: 相比之下，哺乳动物、爬行动物和鸟类都包括可以完全生活在海上而不依赖陆地获取食物或淡水的物种。在此发现之前，科学家们从未发现过具有相同能力的两栖动物的令人信服的化石证据。

paras.en: A Giant Armored Amphibian Built for the Seafloor
paras.zh: 为海底建造的巨型装甲两栖动物

paras.en: Because the two skeletons are so complete, researchers were able to piece together the animal's appearance and develop a clearer picture of how it lived.
paras.zh: 由于这两具骨骼非常完整，研究人员能够拼凑出该动物的外观，并更清晰地了解它的生活方式。

paras.en: Gerrothorax maritimus measured nearly three feet long, but its proportions were far different from those of a modern salamander. Rather than having a long, slender body, it was unusually broad and flattened, with a distinctive disc-shaped form.
paras.zh: Gerrothorax maritimus 长近三英尺，但其比例与现代蝾螈的比例相差甚远。它的身体不是细长的，而是异常宽阔和扁平，具有独特的圆盘状形状。

paras.en: Its body was also covered in thick bony armor, which may have helped protect it from large marine predators such as ichthyosaurs.
paras.zh: 它的身体还覆盖着厚厚的骨甲，这可能有助于保护它免受鱼龙等大型海洋掠食者的侵害。

paras.en: "If you think about today's amphibians, this animal is unusual because it's big," Motani said. "It's probably, body mass-wise, about the same as the giant salamander, but what's different is that giant salamanders are elongated whereas this animal is really chunky."
paras.zh: “如果你想想今天的两栖动物，这种动物很不寻常，因为它很大，”莫塔尼说。 “就体重而言，它可能与大鲵差不多，但不同的是大鲵的体型较长，而这种动物却很矮胖。”

paras.en: The structure of its skull, together with its heavy armor, suggests that this ancient amphibian was an ambush predator. Instead of actively chasing its meals, it likely rested on the seafloor until an unsuspecting animal came within reach.
paras.zh: 它的头骨结构和厚重的盔甲表明这种古老的两栖动物是伏击掠食者。它没有积极地追逐食物，而是在海底休息，直到一只毫无戒心的动物出现在触手可及的地方。

paras.en: "They would probably just wait at the bottom and then when prey comes around, they would just suck it in," said Motani, who noted that the hunting strategy resembles that of the wobbegong, a type of carpet shark that lives near the seafloor and captures prey using suction.
paras.zh: 莫塔尼说：“它们可能只是在海底等待，然后当猎物出现时，它们就会把猎物吸进去。”他指出，这种捕猎策略类似于沃比刚，这是一种生活在海底附近的地毯鲨，利用吸力捕捉猎物。

paras.en: How Could an Amphibian Survive in Salt Water?
paras.zh: 两栖动物如何在盐水中生存？

paras.en: One of the biggest mysteries surrounding Gerrothorax maritimus is how it managed to survive in an environment that is hostile to nearly all modern amphibians.
paras.zh: 围绕Gerrothorax maritimus 的最大谜团之一是它如何在对几乎所有现代两栖动物都充满敌意的环境中生存下来。

paras.en: The problem comes down largely to amphibian skin. Unlike the relatively waterproof skin of many other animals, amphibian skin allows water and gases to pass through it. This makes it useful for breathing and maintaining hydration, but also leaves amphibians especially vulnerable to the effects of salt water.
paras.zh: 这个问题主要归结于两栖动物的皮肤。与许多其他动物相对防水的皮肤不同，两栖动物的皮肤允许水和气体穿过。这使得它有助于呼吸和保持水分，但也使两栖动物特别容易受到盐水的影响。

paras.en: "That skin is permeable, and that allows the animals to use it for multiple purposes," said Motani. "They use it for respiration and water intake, so amphibians don't drink or breathe through the mouth because they can do both through the skin."
paras.zh: “这种皮肤是可渗透的，这使得动物可以将其用于多种目的，”莫塔尼说。 “它们用它来呼吸和饮水，所以两栖动物不会通过嘴喝水或呼吸，因为它们可以通过皮肤完成这两者。”

paras.en: As a result, modern amphibians generally depend on freshwater habitats or environments close to them. A few species have developed limited salt tolerance, including the crab-eating frog. Even these animals can lose weight when exposed to brackish water and must eventually return to freshwater to recover.
paras.zh: 因此，现代两栖动物通常依赖淡水栖息地或靠近它们的环境。一些物种已经产生了有限的耐盐性，包括吃蟹的青蛙。即使这些动物在接触咸水时也会体重减轻，最终必须返回淡水才能恢复。

paras.en: The ancient Gerrothorax maritimus, however, may have evolved a very different solution.
paras.zh: 然而，古代的Gerrothorax maritimus可能进化出了一种非常不同的解决方案。

paras.en: Researchers suggest that its extensive bony armor restricted the movement of water through its skin. This protective covering may have reduced its dependence on absorbing water directly through the skin, allowing the animal to take in seawater through its mouth instead.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，其广泛的骨甲限制了水通过皮肤的流动。这种保护性覆盖物可能减少了它对直接通过皮肤吸收水分的依赖，从而使动物能够通过嘴吸入海水。

paras.en: Under this proposed mechanism, water would have been absorbed through the digestive tract, while the animal's gills could have helped eliminate excess salt. Gills are known to have been present in members of the Gerrothorax genus, giving the researchers reason to suspect that this species possessed a more fishlike approach to managing its salt balance.
paras.zh: 根据这种机制，水可以通过消化道被吸收，而动物的鳃可以帮助消除多余的盐。众所周知，Gerrothorax 属的成员身上存在鳃，这让研究人员有理由怀疑该物种拥有更像鱼类的方法来管理其盐平衡。

paras.en: Together, these adaptations may explain how an amphibian managed to occupy an ecological niche that remains inaccessible to its modern relatives.
paras.zh: 总之，这些适应可以解释两栖动物如何设法占据其现代亲戚无法进入的生态位。

paras.en: Fossil Evidence Points to a Fully Marine Lifestyle
paras.zh: 化石证据表明完全海洋生活方式

paras.en: The researchers also examined whether Gerrothorax maritimus truly lived in the ocean or whether its remains might have been transported there after death.
paras.zh: 研究人员还检查了Gerrothorax maritimus是否真的生活在海洋中，或者它的遗骸是否可能在死后被运送到那里。

paras.en: Several clues strongly favor a marine lifestyle.
paras.zh: 有几条线索强烈支持海洋生活方式。

paras.en: First, the skeletons were recovered from sediments deposited in a deep marine environment. Their remarkable completeness also provides important evidence about where the animals died.
paras.zh: 首先，骨骼是从深海环境中沉积的沉积物中回收的。它们非凡的完整性也提供了有关动物死亡地点的重要证据。

paras.en: "Carcasses at sea, unless they sink to the bottom right away, tend to dry out and lose limbs prior to sinking to the bottom," said Motani. "But these animals had their fingers preserved, so that means they probably died near where they lived."
paras.zh: 莫塔尼说：“海上的尸体除非立即沉入海底，否则在沉入海底之前往往会变干并失去四肢。” “但这些动物的手指被保存下来，这意味着它们可能死在它们居住的地方附近。”

paras.en: The preservation of such delicate skeletal structures suggests that the bodies were not carried long distances before reaching the seafloor.
paras.zh: 如此精致的骨骼结构的保存表明，尸体在到达海底之前并没有被长途运输。

paras.en: To investigate further, the team analyzed the fossils' chemical composition, focusing on the relative abundance of different forms of strontium, known as isotopes.
paras.zh: 为了进一步研究，研究小组分析了化石的化学成分，重点关注不同形式的锶（即同位素）的相对丰度。

paras.en: The results closely matched the strontium isotope signatures expected in ocean water during the Late Triassic, providing another independent line of evidence that the animals inhabited a marine environment.
paras.zh: 结果与三叠纪晚期海水中预期的锶同位素特征非常吻合，为这些动物居住在海洋环境提供了另一条独立的证据。

paras.en: Taken together, the fossil preservation, geological setting, and chemical findings make a compelling case that Gerrothorax maritimus spent its life entirely at sea.
paras.zh: 总而言之，化石保存、地质环境和化学发现令人信服地证明，Gerrothorax maritimus 的一生完全在海上度过。

paras.en: The discovery reveals an unexpected evolutionary path for amphibians, showing that at least one ancient species appears to have overcome the biological limitations that keep its living relatives largely confined to freshwater environments.
paras.zh: 这一发现揭示了两栖动物一条意想不到的进化路径，表明至少一个古老物种似乎已经克服了使其现存亲属主要局限于淡水环境的生物学限制。

paras.en: The research received funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了国家自然科学基金委的资助。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of California - Davis. Original written by Greg Watry. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州大学戴维斯分校提供。原文由格雷格·沃特里撰写。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Lipin Diao, Ryosuke Motani, Da-yong Jiang, Jiaxu Hao, Shengyu Wang. A fully marine stem amphibian from the Late Triassic of China. Nature Ecology, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41559-026-03209-9
paras.zh: - 刁立平、莫谷良介、蒋大勇、郝家旭、王胜宇。一种来自中国晚三叠世的完全海洋茎两栖动物。自然生态学，2026； DOI：10.1038/s41559-026-03209-9

articles.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago

paras.en: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
paras.zh: 科学家发现了一种生活在3400万年前的巨型啮齿动物，重达66磅

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered fossils of a giant rodent that lived in Thailand 34 million years ago, revealing that enormous rodents evolved much earlier than previously thought. Named Yakamys sirindhornae, the ancient animal may have weighed around 66 pounds, roughly twice as much as other known rodents of its time.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了3400万年前生活在泰国的一种巨型啮齿动物的化石，揭示了巨型啮齿动物的进化比之前认为的要早得多。这种古代动物被命名为Yakamys Sirindhornae，体重可能约为 66 磅，大约是当时其他已知啮齿动物的两倍。

paras.en: An ancient rodent of extraordinary size has been identified from fossils uncovered in a mine in southern Thailand. The discovery, made by an international team of paleontologists that includes scientists from McGill University, provides new evidence that giant rodents appeared much earlier and in more parts of the world than previously believed.
paras.zh: 在泰国南部的一个矿井中发现的化石中发现了一种体型非凡的古代啮齿动物。这一发现是由包括麦吉尔大学科学家在内的国际古生物学家团队做出的，它提供了新的证据，表明巨型啮齿类动物的出现时间比之前认为的要早得多，而且出现在世界上更多的地方。

paras.en: The researchers found "remarkably large" fossilized teeth belonging to a previously unknown species called Yakamys sirindhornae. This prehistoric rodent lived approximately 34 million years ago, during the middle of the Paleogene period. Its remains, consisting of a lower second molar and a lower incisor, were recovered from the Bang Mark Pit at the Krabi lignite mine in Thailand's Krabi Province.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现了“非常大”的牙齿化石，属于一种以前未知的物种，称为雅卡米斯水仙鸟。这种史前啮齿动物生活在大约 3400 万年前，古近纪中期。它的遗骸包括一颗下第二臼齿和一颗下门牙，是在泰国甲米省甲米褐煤矿的邦马克坑中发现的。

paras.en: Although only two teeth have been identified, they offer valuable clues about rodent gigantism, the evolutionary process through which rodents develop unusually large bodies. The discovery suggests that Southeast Asia played a more significant role in the early evolution of giant rodents than scientists had recognized.
paras.zh: 虽然只发现了两颗牙齿，但它们提供了有关啮齿类巨型症的宝贵线索，巨型症是啮齿类动物发育出异常巨大身体的进化过程。这一发现表明，东南亚在巨型啮齿动物的早期进化中发挥的作用比科学家们认识到的更为重要。

paras.en: Giant Rodents Have a Much Older History Than Expected
paras.zh: 巨型啮齿动物的历史比预期的要古老得多

paras.en: "Today, the largest living rodent is the capybara, but very large rodents are not restricted to recent ecosystems," said Virginie Millien, a biology professor at McGill University and co-author of the study. "Giant rodents evolved repeatedly during the later history of the group, mostly in South America. This discovery suggests that Southeast Asia also played an important role in the early evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents."
paras.zh: 麦吉尔大学生物学教授、该研究的合著者维吉妮·米利安（Virginie Millien）说：“如今，现存最大的啮齿动物是水豚，但非常大的啮齿动物并不局限于最近的生态系统。” “巨型啮齿动物在该群体的后期历史中反复进化，主要是在南美洲。这一发现表明东南亚在大型啮齿动物的早期进化史上也发挥了重要作用。”

paras.en: The newly identified animal's name reflects both its impressive size and its connection to Thailand. Yakamys combines "yak," the Thai word for giant, with "mys," the Greek word for mouse or rat.
paras.zh: 这种新发现的动物的名字既反映了它令人印象深刻的体型，也反映了它与泰国的联系。 Yakamys 将“yak”（泰语中“巨人”的意思）与“mys”（希腊语中“老鼠”的意思）结合在一起。

paras.en: The second part of its scientific name recognizes an important supporter of scientific research in Thailand.
paras.zh: 其学名的第二部分表彰了泰国科学研究的重要支持者。

paras.en: "The species name, sirindhornae, honors Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, in recognition of her longstanding support for science and paleontological research in Thailand," Millien said.
paras.zh: 米利恩说：“这个物种的名字，诗琳通，是为了纪念诗琳通公主，以表彰她长期以来对泰国科学和古生物学研究的支持。”

paras.en: How Big Was This 34-Million-Year-Old Rodent?
paras.zh: 这种 3400 万年前的啮齿动物有多大？

paras.en: To estimate the animal's size, the research team applied seven established methods that use tooth measurements to calculate body mass. Their results suggest that Yakamys sirindhornae weighed approximately 30 kilograms, making it about twice as heavy as other known rodents from the same period, including Hulgana.
paras.zh: 为了估计动物的大小，研究小组应用了七种既定的方法，利用牙齿测量来计算体重。他们的研究结果表明，Yakamys Sirindhornae 重约 30 公斤，是同时期其他已知啮齿动物（包括 Hulgana）的两倍。

paras.en: That would have made the newly discovered species exceptionally large compared with its contemporaries. However, the researchers emphasize that determining an extinct animal's weight from a small number of fossilized teeth involves considerable uncertainty.
paras.zh: 与同时代的物种相比，这将使新发现的物种异常庞大。然而，研究人员强调，从少量牙齿化石确定灭绝动物的重量存在相当大的不确定性。

paras.en: "This is only a ballpark figure, as there is substantial uncertainty associated with fossil body-mass estimation," Millien said.
paras.zh: 米利恩说：“这只是一个大概的数字，因为化石体重估计存在很大的不确定性。”

paras.en: The limited fossil evidence also makes it difficult to reconstruct how Yakamys evolved or what its life was like. Additional discoveries will be needed to better understand its physical characteristics, ecological role, and evolutionary relationships.
paras.zh: 有限的化石证据也使得很难重建雅卡米斯如何进化或其生活是什么样的。需要更多的发现来更好地了解其物理特征、生态作用和进化关系。

paras.en: International Research Uncovers Thailand's Prehistoric Past
paras.zh: 国际研究揭示泰国的史前历史

paras.en: The fossils were identified through an ongoing international collaboration investigating ancient mammals in Thailand's Krabi Basin. The project brings together scientists from McGill University, Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources, and French research organizations, including CNRS and Université de Poitiers.
paras.zh: 这些化石是通过一项正在进行的国际合作调查泰国甲米盆地的古代哺乳动物而发现的。该项目汇集了来自麦吉尔大学、泰国矿产资源部以及法国国家科学研究中心和普瓦捷大学等法国研究组织的科学家。

paras.en: By revealing evidence of an unusually large rodent in Southeast Asia 34 million years ago, the discovery expands scientists' understanding of where and when rodent gigantism emerged. Future fossil finds could help establish how these ancient giants lived and how their evolution relates to the enormous rodents that appeared elsewhere in the world.
paras.zh: 通过揭示 3400 万年前东南亚存在一种异常大型啮齿动物的证据，这一发现扩大了科学家对啮齿动物巨型现象出现的地点和时间的了解。未来的化石发现可以帮助确定这些古代巨人如何生活，以及它们的进化与世界其他地方出现的巨型啮齿动物有何关系。

paras.en: The research received support from CNRS, Université de Poitiers, Université de Montpellier, McGill University, and the Department of Mineral Resources of Thailand.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了法国国家科学研究中心、普瓦捷大学、蒙彼利埃大学、麦吉尔大学和泰国矿产资源部的支持。

paras.en: Materials provided by McGill University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由麦吉尔大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Yaowalak Chaimanee, Laurent Marivaux, Virginie Millien, Chotima Yamee, Pannipa Tian, Jean-Jacques Jaeger. A giant eocene ischyromyid from Southeast Asia reveals the early evolution of rodent gigantism. Scientific Reports, 2026; 16 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-76711-6
paras.zh: - Yaowalak Chaimanee、Laurent Marivaux、Virginie Millien、Chotima Yamee、Pannipa Tian、Jean-Jacques Jaeger。来自东南亚的始新世巨齿鲨揭示了啮齿动物巨人症的早期进化。科学报告，2026； 16 (1) DOI：10.1038/s41598-026-76711-6

articles.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't

paras.en: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
paras.zh: 科学家发现为什么有些蚊子爱你而另一些蚊子不爱你

paras.en: - A surprising new study reveals that mosquitoes have very different tastes in humans, with each species attracted to its own combination of skin odors, chemicals, and bacteria. The discovery challenges the idea of a universal mosquito magnet and could lead to more effective repellents against dangerous disease-spreading mosquitoes.
paras.zh: - 一项令人惊讶的新研究表明，蚊子对人类的口味截然不同，每个物种都会被自己的皮肤气味、化学物质和细菌的组合所吸引。这一发现挑战了通用蚊子磁体的想法，并可能导致更有效的驱虫剂来对抗传播疾病的危险蚊子。

paras.en: Some people seem to attract mosquitoes wherever they go, but new research reveals that being a mosquito magnet depends on which species is doing the biting.
paras.zh: 有些人似乎无论走到哪里都会吸引蚊子，但新的研究表明，蚊子的吸引力取决于叮咬的物种。

paras.en: In a study published in iScience, researchers at Florida International University (FIU) tested how three of the world's most dangerous mosquito species responded to 119 human volunteers. Surprisingly, not a single participant attracted all three species. Instead, each species favored a different group of people, largely based on their individual body chemistry and natural skin odors.
paras.zh: 在《iScience》杂志上发表的一项研究中，佛罗里达国际大学 (FIU) 的研究人员测试了世界上最危险的三种蚊子对 119 名人类志愿者的反应。令人惊讶的是，没有一个参与者吸引了所有三个物种。相反，每个物种都偏爱不同的人群，这很大程度上取决于他们各自的身体化学成分和自然皮肤气味。

paras.en: The discovery could change how scientists approach the prevention of mosquito-borne diseases. Because different mosquito species respond to different chemical signals from human skin, researchers may eventually be able to create next-generation, species-specific repellents that offer more targeted protection.
paras.zh: 这一发现可能会改变科学家预防蚊媒疾病的方式。由于不同的蚊子种类对人类皮肤发出的不同化学信号有不同的反应，研究人员最终可能能够创造出下一代、针对特定物种的驱虫剂，提供更有针对性的保护。

paras.en: "Isolating the components of human odor that attract or repel mosquitoes could lead to novel strategies to combat vector-borne diseases," said Matthew DeGennaro, a neurogeneticist who leads the research team and directs the Biomolecular Sciences Institute at FIU, Miami's state university.
paras.zh: “分离出吸引或驱除蚊子的人类气味成分可能会带来对抗媒介传播疾病的新策略，”领导该研究团队并领导迈阿密州立大学佛罗里达国际大学生物分子科学研究所的神经遗传学家马修·德根纳罗（Matthew DeGennaro）说。

paras.en: Different Mosquito Species Prefer Different People
paras.zh: 不同种类的蚊子喜欢不同的人

paras.en: The researchers investigated three species responsible for spreading serious illnesses, including yellow fever, dengue, Zika, West Nile and other diseases. These were Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) and Culex quinquefasciatus (southern house mosquito).
paras.zh: 研究人员调查了三种传播严重疾病的物种，包括黄热病、登革热、寨卡病毒、西尼罗河病毒和其他疾病。这些是埃及伊蚊、白纹伊蚊（亚洲虎蚊）和致倦库蚊（南方家蚊）。

paras.en: Led by Ph.D. student Kaylee Marrero, the investigation was the first to directly compare how several mosquito species reacted to the same human participants. The findings revealed unexpected differences in the chemical and microbial signals each species appeared to use when choosing whom to bite.
paras.zh: 由博士领导。学生凯莉·马雷罗（Kaylee Marrero）表示，这项调查首次直接比较了几种蚊子对同一人类参与者的反应。研究结果揭示了每个物种在选择咬谁时似乎使用的化学和微生物信号存在意想不到的差异。

paras.en: "We didn't expect the species to prefer different people when we started the study," Marrero said. "Each species having a distinct microbial signature that they use as a cue was so surprising to me."
paras.zh: “当我们开始研究时，我们并没有想到该物种会喜欢不同的人，”马雷罗说。 “每个物种都有独特的微生物特征，并以此作为线索，这让我感到非常惊讶。”

paras.en: Each mosquito species showed its own distinct preferences:
paras.zh: 每种蚊子都有自己独特的偏好：

paras.en: - Aedes aegypti: This species favored people who were not wearing added fragrances and whose skin contained lower levels of certain volatile chemical compounds. It typically bites during the day and showed a slight preference for men over women.
paras.zh: - 埃及伊蚊：该物种喜欢不使用添加香料且皮肤中某些挥发性化合物含量较低的人。它通常在白天咬人，并且对男性的偏好略高于对女性的偏好。

paras.en: - Aedes albopictus: Also known as the Asian tiger mosquito, this daytime feeder was particularly attracted to people whose skin released higher levels of ketones and naturally occurring plant-like volatile compounds.
paras.zh: - 白纹伊蚊：也被称为亚洲虎蚊，这种白天捕食者特别容易被那些皮肤释放较高水平酮和天然植物性挥发性化合物的人所吸引。

paras.en: - Culex quinquefasciatus: Unlike the other two species, the southern house mosquito feeds after dark and appeared especially sensitive to the skin microbiome, the community of bacteria, fungi, and other microorganisms that naturally inhabit human skin. Certain bacterial families made people more attractive, while others seemed to discourage the mosquitoes from biting.
paras.zh: - 致倦库蚊（Culex quinquefasciatus）：与其他两种蚊子不同，南方家蚊在天黑后进食，并且对皮肤微生物群（自然栖息在人类皮肤上的细菌、真菌和其他微生物群落）特别敏感。某些细菌家族使人更具吸引力，而另一些细菌家族似乎阻止蚊子叮咬。

paras.en: The Hidden Chemistry Behind Mosquito Attraction
paras.zh: 吸引蚊子背后隐藏的化学成分

paras.en: Human body odor is far more complicated than it might seem. Our skin releases a mixture of more than 1,000 volatile organic compounds, many of which scientists have yet to fully identify or understand.
paras.zh: 人体的气味比看起来要复杂得多。我们的皮肤会释放 1,000 多种挥发性有机化合物的混合物，其中许多化合物尚未被科学家完全识别或理解。

paras.en: The researchers found that the three mosquito species did not share a common preference for particular individuals. Instead, each consistently favored its own subset of volunteers, suggesting that different species have evolved distinct methods for detecting and interpreting human scent.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这三种蚊子对特定个体没有共同的偏好。相反，每个物种都始终偏爱自己的志愿者子集，这表明不同的物种已经进化出不同的方法来检测和解释人类气味。

paras.en: To investigate what made certain people more appealing, the team collected samples of participants' body odors and skin microbiomes alongside the mosquito preference tests. They then examined which chemical compounds and microorganisms were present and measured their relative abundance.
paras.zh: 为了调查是什么让某些人更具吸引力，研究小组在进行蚊子偏好测试的同时，还收集了参与者的体味和皮肤微生物组样本。然后他们检查了存在的化学物质和微生物，并测量了它们的相对丰度。

paras.en: The results showed strong connections between the mosquitoes' preferences and differences in the chemical and microbial makeup of people's skin.
paras.zh: 结果表明，蚊子的偏好与人们皮肤化学和微生物组成的差异之间存在密切联系。

paras.en: "This connected so well with the differences in skin bacteria and odors," DeGennaro said. "It is clear to me now that our skin microbiomes define our human odor signature. Each species found its own way to decode that signature."
paras.zh: “这与皮肤细菌和气味的差异密切相关，”德根纳罗说。 “现在我很清楚，我们的皮肤微生物组定义了我们的人类气味特征。每个物种都找到了自己的方式来解码该特征。”

paras.en: Could This Discovery Lead to Better Mosquito Repellents?
paras.zh: 这一发现能否带来更好的驱蚊剂？

paras.en: Understanding why one mosquito species finds a person attractive while another does not could open new possibilities for preventing dangerous infections.
paras.zh: 了解为什么一种蚊子认为一个人有吸引力，而另一种蚊子则不然，这可能为预防危险感染开辟新的可能性。

paras.en: By identifying the specific chemical compounds and skin bacteria that attract or discourage different mosquitoes, the FIU researchers are helping establish a scientific foundation for more precisely targeted repellents.
paras.zh: 通过识别吸引或阻止不同蚊子的特定化合物和皮肤细菌，佛罗里达国际大学的研究人员正在帮助建立更精确的针对性驱虫剂的科学基础。

paras.en: The findings could also improve public health strategies by allowing communities to focus on the particular mosquito species responsible for spreading disease in their region.
paras.zh: 研究结果还可以通过让社区关注负责在其地区传播疾病的特定蚊子种类来改善公共卫生策略。

paras.en: Rather than assuming that all mosquitoes are drawn to the same people for the same reasons, future prevention methods may be designed around the distinct chemical preferences of each species.
paras.zh: 未来的预防方法可能会围绕每个物种不同的化学偏好来设计，而不是假设所有蚊子都出于相同的原因被同一个人所吸引。

paras.en: Materials provided by Florida International University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由佛罗里达国际大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Kaylee M. Marrero, John S. Castillo, Dani Lucas-Barbosa, Anthony J. Bellantuono, Matthew A. Marrero, Dariel Cid, Andre L. Costa-da-Silva, Niels O. Verhulst, Matthew DeGennaro. Individual humans are more attractive to certain mosquito species. iScience, 2026; 29 (8): 117006 DOI: 10.1016/j.isci.2026.117006
paras.zh: - 凯莉·M·马雷罗、约翰·S·卡斯蒂略、丹尼·卢卡斯-巴博萨、安东尼·J·贝兰图诺、马修·A·马雷罗、达里尔·西德、安德烈·L·科斯塔-达·席尔瓦、尼尔斯·O·维赫斯特、马修·德根纳罗。人类个体对某些蚊子物种更有吸引力。 i科学，2026； 29（8）：117006 DOI：10.1016/j.isci.2026.117006

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field.
paras.zh: 2013 年 11 月 10 日，欧洲的 GOCE 卫星在轨道上运行四年、绘制地球引力场图后坠落地球。

paras.en: GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel.
paras.zh: GOCE 是重力场和稳态海洋环流探测器的缩写，于 2009 年发射，其任务是以前所未有的方式绘制地球重力图。但尽管任务取得了成功，它还是在 2013 年燃料耗尽而宣告失败。

paras.en: At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth. Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage.
paras.zh: 当时，控制人员不确定 GOCE 会在何处返回地球。有些人担心它可能会坠入人口稠密的地区。不过，小型航天器在大气层中解体，并未造成任何财产损失。

paras.en: It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity, mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents.
paras.zh: 它在南大西洋福克兰群岛上空约 50 英里处解体。欧洲航天局称这次任务取得了成功。 GOCE 的持续时间远远超出预期。它显示了地球重力的微小变化，绘制了地壳和地幔的结构图，并跟踪了洋流。

paras.en: The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname.
paras.zh: GOCE 卫星是一艘时尚的航天器，其鳍片覆盖着太阳能电池板，使其具有未来派的设计。事实上，它的外观为它赢得了一个很酷的绰号。

paras.en: "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description.
paras.zh: “GOCE 时尚、优雅的空气动力学设计——使其被称为‘太空法拉利’——立即使其与大多数其他卫星区分开来。”欧空局官员在一份描述中表示。

paras.en: There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude.
paras.zh: GOCE 的设计背后不仅仅有外观。为了生成有史以来最好的地球引力场图，GOCE 必须在如此低的轨道上飞行——只有 139 英里（224 公里）——它需要抵消该高度地球薄薄大气层的阻力。国际空间站绕地球运行的高度几乎是该高度的两倍。

paras.en: GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space, leading to a fiery plunge to Earth.
paras.zh: GOCE 由氙离子发动机提供动力，可以在低轨道上保持四年。一旦燃料耗尽，这颗重达一吨的卫星就无法维持其在太空中的位置，导致猛烈坠向地球。

paras.en: The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface.
paras.zh: GOCE 的体积较大——重 2,425 磅（1,100 公斤）、长 17 英尺（5.3 米）、宽 3.2 英尺（1 m）——使其再入过程引人注目，特别是因为预计该卫星至少 25% 的部分将到达地球表面。

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。
